d: A relocatable foundation that becomes a Travel Anchor with a Temporal Crystal or a Cargo Anchor with a Cargo Transmitter.
x:
Anchor

The Anchor is a private foundation for either travel or cargo infrastructure.

Construction
Craft it from three bronze plates, a Temporal Gear, two pieces of clear quartz, one Temporal Residue, and two full rock blocks. Tin bronze, bismuth bronze, and black bronze plates are interchangeable. Full natural rock blocks may use any supported stone type; loose stones are not accepted.

Calibration and Specialization
Placement begins a five-second calibration. Once ready, install a Temporal Crystal to create a charged Travel Anchor or a Cargo Transmitter to create a Cargo Anchor. Each player may maintain one of each specialized role.

Relocation
Hold Sneak while placing an Anchor to relocate your existing unassigned foundation or Travel Anchor remotely. Relocation preserves the Anchor item rather than consuming it. A Travel Anchor also transfers its installed Crystal and charge. Cargo Anchors are never relocated remotely: empty and break them manually before establishing another. Breaking a Cargo Anchor returns its installed Cargo Transmitter.

Controlled Travel
When the HUD reports Travel: Ready, hold right-click with the Temporal Triangulator in Anchor mode and remain still through synchronization. Successful travel returns you beside the Travel Anchor. An uncharged Crystal is consumed for one return; charged Crystals instead spend one sixth of full capacity per jump. Releasing early, moving too far, or losing a valid destination cancels without consuming charge.

Ownership and Destruction
Only the owner or a privileged administrator may break a bound Anchor. Manually breaking a Travel Anchor returns its installed Temporal Crystal, including a depleted reusable Crystal, to inventory or drops it nearby. Explosions and unusual removal can still destroy the charge. A dropped Anchor does not retain ownership or calibration.

Disposable and Reusable Crystals
An uncharged Crystal powers one Anchor return and is consumed by that jump. A charged Crystal instead spends one sixth of its full capacity per return and remains reusable after depletion. Failed travel refunds reserved charge. Sneak-use the Anchor with an empty hand to remove its reusable Crystal, then recharge it in the Rift Resonance Array. Remove the installed reusable Crystal before inserting another or converting the Anchor to cargo. A partially charged Crystal needs enough energy for a whole jump to be installed.

x:

d: A private six-slot field transmitter. Bind it to your calibrated Cargo Anchor using the Temporal Triangulator in Cargo Anchor mode.
x:
Cargo Transmitter

A portable temporal cargo component with two uses.

Cargo Anchor Installation
Use a Cargo Transmitter on a calibrated, unassigned Anchor foundation to install it as the receiving component and convert the foundation into your Cargo Anchor.

Field Transmitter
Place a second Cargo Transmitter in the world. Its front automatically faces you when placed and it provides six staging slots. Select Cargo Anchor mode on the Temporal Triangulator and use it on the placed Transmitter to bind the field endpoint to your Cargo Anchor.

See Temporal Cargo for transmission and compatibility guidance.

d: A reusable glass-and-metal core built to receive a captured blue rift. Hold Sneak and use a block face to place it for display.
x:
Containment Core

A reusable reinforced vessel for captured temporal disturbances.

Install an empty Containment Core in a Rift Harvester. Place the prepared Harvester within ten blocks of a natural Temporal Rift or stabilized blue Convergence Rift, select Rift mode on the Temporal Triangulator, and complete the scan. Capturing a natural Rift produces a Rift Core. Capturing a blue Convergence Rift produces a Stabilized Rift Core.

The empty Core may also be installed decoratively in a Rift Core Sconce or placed for display by holding Sneak while using a block face.

The Rift Resonance Array returns this empty vessel only when a Rift Core reaches 0%. A Core with energy left remains a Rift Core and can charge another Crystal.

d: An eye-level control housing with separate sockets for a Stabilized Rift Core and a Temporal Crystal.
x:
Convergence Core Housing

The control center of a Convergence Gate. Place it in any non-corner perimeter position where a Conflux Frame Block would go, including the top or bottom. Face its control panel outward so it remains accessible.

Its two sockets accept one Stabilized Rift Core and one charged Temporal Crystal for paired travel. A natural Rift Core instead provides Exploration Rift behavior. Open the Housing to name the gate, select a destination, and configure public or private access. Removing either installed component safely collapses the contained rift.

Crystal Budget
Paired travel spends one sixth of full Crystal charge at the departure Gate only. A full Crystal supports six departures; with the default capacity each costs five minutes. The destination must be powered but pays no arrival cost. A depleted or insufficiently charged Crystal stays in the Housing for removal and recharging in the Rift Resonance Array. Charge is refunded if arrival fails.

Owner-only controls include the known-player list, Public/Private access, and confirmed ownership transfer. Visitors see travel information and power, not settings. Remove any Recovery Core and finish transit before transferring ownership. Destination Standby means a remote Gate awaits loading. See Convergence Gates for access, protection, and safe-arrival rules.

d: A prototype Core tuned to hold open a green passage into The Fractured Deep.

Dimensional Core

A prototype Core tuned to The Fractured Deep, a persistent realm carried by Manifold.

First Test
Install the Core in a complete Convergence Gate together with a charged Temporal Crystal. The Gate forms a green rift. Entering spends one normal Gate jump and places you at the Threshold in The Fractured Deep.

A second green rift near the Threshold returns you to safe ground beside the Gate you entered through. Returning does not spend another Crystal jump.

This first research prototype is available through the creative inventory while its survival acquisition path is being developed.

Death and Return
Dying in The Fractured Deep returns your next respawn to the Threshold beside its green return rift. Drops stay at the death location. This does not permanently change your ordinary overworld spawn.

Preview Limits
Bring a light source. Natural rifts can appear inside the realm. Chart is an optional separate mapping mod, not bundled. Official Chart compatibility is being tested; cavern-floor mapping is not guaranteed. Unwanted daylight in some generated areas remains a known lighting limitation.

d: A one-use Core that remembers its owner's next death and opens a return rift at a Convergence Gate.
x:
Recovery Core

A one-use Core that records its owner's next death and powers a return through a Convergence Gate. It works without XSkills.

Make an Offering
Put a fully charged natural Rift Core in your offhand and a knife in your main hand. Sneak and hold Use for two seconds. The offering transforms the Rift Core, costs 2 health and 1 knife durability, and consumes the configured amount of temporal stability: 80 percentage points by default. You need more than 2 health and at least that much stability before beginning. All Core types can be held in the offhand, but only a full natural Rift Core accepts this offering.

Arm Your Gate
Open a completed Gate and install the Recovery Core plus a charged Temporal Crystal with enough energy for one Gate jump. The Core binds to the Gate owner; if the Gate is unclaimed, the player who opened it becomes the owner. Only one installed Recovery Core can be armed for an owner at a time. A purple standby rift and Awaiting Owner Death status confirm readiness. Standby cannot transport anyone and does not change your normal respawn point.

Record and Store
The installed Core records the owner's next death in the Gate's dimension, even if the Gate's chunk is unloaded. Later deaths do not overwrite that location. The Gate portal changes to orange when the return is ready; the Core itself stays purple. Its tooltip shows the owner and recorded death coordinates and dimension. You can remove and store a recorded Core, then reinstall it in a Gate you own when ready to return. The imprint stays on that Core across storage and saving. A removed Core cannot record a new death.

Return
After respawning, enter the orange rift in your prepared Gate. Only the bound owner may use it. The Gate looks for safe ground near the recorded death. A successful arrival spends one configured Gate jump and turns the Recovery Core into an empty Containment Core. At default settings this costs five minutes of Crystal charge. If no safe landing can be found, the imprint and Crystal charge remain available. Your death drops stay where they fell; the Core does not collect them.

Arrival Protection
A successful return grants 8 seconds of damage protection by default, with a visible countdown. Use that time to reach safety. Attacking ends protection early. Reconnecting does not restart it.

Server Settings
Admins can use F8 or /rt menu, then Settings, Server, Recovery to change the offering's stability cost (0-100%) and arrival protection (0-30 seconds; 0 disables protection).

d: A captured natural Rift holding up to 100% charge for the Rift Resonance Array. Unused charging energy remains in the Core.
x:
Rift Core

A natural Temporal Rift captured by a prepared Rift Harvester during a completed Rift-mode scan.

Percentage Charge
A newly captured Core starts at 100%. In the Rift Resonance Array, 100% supplies one full Temporal Crystal of energy. Topping up a Crystal uses only its missing charge and leaves the unused percentage in the Core. For example, filling a Crystal from 20% to 100% uses 80% of a full Core and leaves 20%. Core tooltips and Array or placed-Core information show the remaining percentage.

If the Core runs out before the Crystal is full, the Crystal retains the energy transferred. Replace the empty Containment Core with another Rift Core to finish. Only a fully depleted Core becomes an empty Containment Core. Core energy survives removal, saving, placement, pickup, and breaking its placed display.

Other Uses
Install it in a Rift Core Sconce for temporal light, or Sneak-use a block face to place it for display. In a constructed Gate, a natural Core provides Exploration Rift behavior rather than a paired destination link; that process consumes the captured rift and returns its empty vessel. A fully charged natural Rift Core can also be transformed through a knife offering; see Recovery Core for the ritual and its costs. Use a Stabilized Rift Core for paired Convergence Gate travel. Natural Rift Cores do not provide passive warding.

d: A compact wall cradle that provides temporal lighting and turns an installed Stabilized Rift Core into a passive Rift Ward.
x:
Rift Core Sconce

A compact Anchor-style wall cradle for displaying and using captured rifts as base lighting.

Placement
Use the Sconce on a vertical block face. It automatically faces away from the supporting wall.

Core Installation
Use an empty Containment Core, Rift Core, or Stabilized Rift Core on the mounted Sconce to install it. An empty Containment Core is decorative and emits no light. A Rift Core produces steady temporal light. A Stabilized Rift Core produces stronger cyan light and automatically becomes a passive Rift Ward. Use the Sconce with an empty hand to remove the installed core.

Passive Rift Ward
An installed Stabilized Rift Core suppresses 97.5% of newly forming natural rifts within a 50-block horizontal radius. It consumes no Temporal Gears or temporal charge. The Sconce reports how many rifts it has warded. Existing rifts, creatures, temporal storms, personal temporal stability, and intentional blue Convergence Rifts are unaffected. Removing the Stabilized Rift Core immediately disables the ward. Warding is enabled by default. Admins can toggle Sconce rift warding in F8 or /rt menu under Settings, Server, Rifts. Disabling warding keeps the Sconce usable as a light and display.

Safety
Breaking the Sconce returns both the holder and its installed core.

d: Captures natural Temporal Rifts and stabilized blue Convergence Rifts into an installed Containment Core when scanned in Rift mode. Travel mode never harvests.
x:
Rift Harvester

A prepared capture apparatus for natural Temporal Rifts and stabilized blue Convergence Rifts.

Install one empty Containment Core, then place the Harvester within ten blocks of the target rift. Select Rift mode on the Temporal Triangulator and maintain the scan until completion. A natural Rift becomes a Rift Core; a blue Convergence Rift becomes a Stabilized Rift Core. Travel mode never harvests.

Use the Harvester with an empty hand to remove the completed core. Breaking the Harvester safely packs its installed core with it.

d: A six-station workshop machine that transfers captured Rift Core energy into depleted or partially charged Temporal Crystals. Requires a clear 5 x 5 area, three blocks high, on solid ground.
x:
Rift Resonance Array

A permanent workshop machine for transferring captured rift energy into Temporal Crystals. Craft one controller with eight Conflux Iron plates, six Temporal Glass blocks, six Containment Insulators, six Conflux Iron rods, and one Temporal Gear.

Placement
Place at the centre of a clear, dry 5 x 5 area with three blocks of headroom and a solid floor. The control panel faces you. The packed controller unfolds into the complete machine. Its lid lowers into the temporal glow at ground level while the machinery rises into place. Allow deployment to finish before using the stations.

Charging
Use a station with one depleted or partially charged Temporal Crystal and one natural Rift Core. The Array automatically processes ready stations in clockwise order: three seconds to spin up, a transfer time proportional to the energy supplied, three seconds to spin down, then two seconds to unlock. A full refill always takes sixty seconds of transfer, regardless of the server-configured Crystal capacity; a 50% refill takes thirty seconds and a 10% refill takes six seconds. If the Core has less energy than the Crystal needs, transfer time follows the available Core energy. Small top-ups can finish their transfer in a fraction of a second; alignment and cooldown still take their normal time. A full Rift Core supplies one full Crystal of charge. Top-ups consume only the missing percentage; unused energy remains in the Core. If a Core runs out first, the Crystal keeps the transferred charge. Four Residue are deposited when a Crystal reaches full charge. Only a fully depleted Rift Core becomes an empty Containment Core for reuse. Stabilized Rift Cores power Gates, Sconce wards, and Storm Stabilizers; they cannot charge Crystals in the Array.

Unloading
Use an empty hand to remove the Crystal. Sneak-use an empty hand to select the Core instead. The active station stays locked until its cycle finishes; the other stations remain accessible. Look at a station or use the controller to read its status.

Persistence
Contents and progress survive saving and reloading. Processing pauses while part of the structure is unloaded. Breaking any part dismantles the Array and returns its contents once; manual survival breaking also returns the controller. Crystals retain their remaining time and Cores retain their unused percentage when removed, saved, placed, or picked up.

Reading the Machine
The outer center platform turns clockwise toward the selected station. Its radial lines glow during charging, while the inner rotor spins independently. A glowing Crystal may still have room for a top-up: check its remaining time against full capacity. Core information shows its remaining percentage. The rift and active line glow collapse after the transfer, and the Array advances to the next ready station or returns to idle.

Residue Tray
Each Crystal reaching full charge deposits four Temporal Residue in the small base tray near the central rift. Use the tray with an empty hand to collect. An incomplete transfer gives no completion Residue.

Charged Crystals also extend the protective radius of a Temporal Storm Stabilizer.

Legacy Placement Recovery
If an upgraded world has invisible reservations blocking placement, ask a server admin to stand near the affected Array site and run /rtarraycleanup. It removes obsolete worksite reservations and orphaned Array proxies nearby; it does not remove proxies belonging to a valid loaded Array. Back up the world before repairs.

d: A harvested blue Convergence Rift used for passive warding or to power a linked Convergence Gate.
x:
Stabilized Rift Core

A stabilized blue Convergence Rift captured by a prepared Rift Harvester while the Temporal Triangulator is in Rift mode. Keep an empty Containment Core installed in the Harvester within ten blocks of the blue Rift. Without a prepared Harvester, a six-second Rift-mode hold collapses the convergence for Residue instead and produces no Core.

Install it in a Rift Core Sconce to create a passive Rift Ward, or install it in the Core socket of a Convergence Gate. The same Core cannot serve multiple machines at once. It may also be placed for display by holding Sneak while using a block face.

Paired Gates also require a charged Temporal Crystal, which supplies the six-jump travel budget. Stabilized Cores are not Array charging fuel; use a natural Rift Core to charge Crystals.

Storm Stabilizer
One Stabilized Rift Core also powers the Temporal Storm Stabilizer. It is not consumed. Stop the machine, wait for its arms to fold, then sneak-right-click the central structure with an empty hand to retrieve it.

d: An iron bloom infused with unstable temporal energy. Heat and work it on an iron anvil to consolidate Conflux Iron.

Temporal Bloom

A porous Iron Bloom infused throughout with Temporal Solvent. Unstable green energy remains trapped among its slag and cavities.

Heat the Temporal Bloom above 700°C, place it on an iron-tier anvil, and work it using the Conflux Iron ingot smithing recipe. Consolidating the bloom removes unstable slag and aligns its temporal inclusions into one Conflux Iron ingot.

Optional Prosequor Integration
Removing slag on an anvil awards Metalworking XP with Prosequor installed: 0.01 XP per removed slag voxel by default, not per hammer strike or completed ingot. Prosequor handles normal metal-shaping XP separately. Admins can adjust the slag reward in F8 or /rt menu, Settings, Server, Prosequor.

d: Stores reusable charge for Temporal Drives and up to six Anchor or paired Gate jumps when full. Empty and partial Crystals can be charged in the Rift Resonance Array.
x:
Temporal Crystal

Condensed temporal energy produced through advanced Temporal Retort research. Review confirmed protocols in Temporal Discoveries or with /rt discoveries.

Crystal Charge
A fully charged Crystal holds 30 minutes of energy by default. Item and machine information shows remaining time and available jumps. Server settings can change the full duration. Anchor and paired Gate travel each require one sixth of a full charge: five minutes by default, allowing six jumps from a full Crystal. Charge also spent in a Temporal Drive reduces the jumps available. A partially charged Crystal with less than one jump remaining must be topped up before travel.

Charging and Appearance
Use the Rift Resonance Array with a natural Rift Core to charge an empty Crystal or top up a partially charged one. A Crystal with any energy uses the luminous charged model; this does not necessarily mean it is full or has enough energy for a jump. At zero it uses the uncharged model. Remaining energy survives inventory storage, drops, placement and pickup, machine insertion and removal, saving, and Anchor relocation.

Temporal Drive
The Drive consumes charge continuously while loaded and running, even without a connected load. It stops at zero and retains the Crystal for empty-hand removal. Time spent paused or unloaded does not drain it.

Disposable and Reusable Crystals
An uncharged Crystal powers one Anchor return and is consumed by that jump. A charged Crystal instead spends one sixth of its full capacity per return and remains reusable after depletion. Failed travel refunds reserved charge. Sneak-use the Anchor with an empty hand to remove its reusable Crystal, then recharge it in the Rift Resonance Array. Remove the installed reusable Crystal before inserting another or converting the Anchor to cargo. A partially charged Crystal needs enough energy for a whole jump to be installed.

Paired Convergence Gates
Install a charged Crystal beside a Stabilized Rift Core. Each departure spends one jump from the departure Gate only. The receiving Gate must also be powered but pays no arrival cost. A housing retains its depleted Crystal for removal and recharging; failed travel refunds reserved charge.

Storm Protection
Install empty or charged Crystals in the four pedestals of a Temporal Storm Stabilizer. Each adds 4 blocks of full-strength radius plus up to 8 more according to its charge, with default settings. Charge is retained during Stabilizer operation; recharge removed Crystals in the Array.

Temporal Quartz

Quartz infused through Temporal Retort research. Smelt four pieces at 1420 degrees in a vanilla Bloomery to produce two Temporal Glass blocks. With IndustrialStory installed, instead load four pieces into its Small Smelter, add fuel, and keep a Bellows working. The IndustrialStory recipe begins at 1100 degrees and produces the same two blocks; break the Smelter Base after it finishes to collect them.

d: Coarse crystalline deposits recovered from ancient temporal mechanisms.
x:
Temporal Residue

Coarse crystalline deposits recovered from temporal machinery and rift activity. A discoverable clamped Temporal Retort protocol can strip four Residue from one Temporal Gear while recovering its cleaned mechanism as a Rusty Gear. Review Temporal Discoveries for the exact reaction conditions after confirming the protocol.

Residue from Rift Analysis and Travel
Collapsing a successfully analyzed natural Rift leaves two measures of Temporal Residue on the Temporal Triangulator. Successful random travel through a stabilized natural Convergence Rift leaves four additional measures. The instrument can hold twelve measures. Failed travel, controlled Anchor travel, constructed Convergence Gate travel, and cargo transmission produce no buildup.

To recover accumulated Residue, select the Triangulator's Residue Extraction mode, aim into open air, and use it. The recovered material enters your inventory or drops nearby if no space is available.

Process the Residue in a Quern to refine it one-for-one into Temporal Dust.

Rift Resonance Array
Each Crystal that reaches full charge in the Rift Resonance Array deposits four Residue in the small collection tray on the base near the central rift. Use the tray with an empty hand to collect. A transfer that leaves the Crystal only partially charged awards no completion Residue. Uncollected Residue survives saving and is returned when the Array is dismantled.

The liquid is consumed as a reaction medium in discoverable protocols including Temporal Gear extraction, rust condensation, and Conflux Iron infusion. A Conflux storm-protection machine with a removable Stabilized Rift Core and four optional Crystal pedestals. Its spherical shield grows with field strength and installed Crystal charge: 16 to 64 blocks of radius at full strength with default settings.

Read Temporal Storm Stabilizer for placement, controls, Crystal combinations, protection limits, and shutdown.

d: A multi-mode instrument. Rift mode scans and harvests; Travel mode activates blue Convergence Rifts. It can be stored on compatible tool racks.
x:
An experimental instrument designed to detect, harvest, and safely traverse temporal disturbances.

Operating Modes
Press F to change tool mode.

Rift Mode
Scans natural rifts and records triangulation locks. A prepared Rift Harvester within ten blocks captures the scanned rift into its installed Containment Core. At a stabilized blue Convergence Rift, a prepared Harvester within ten blocks takes priority and captures a Stabilized Rift Core. Without one, aim from within ten blocks and hold Right mouse for approximately six seconds to collapse the Rift and store up to four Temporal Residue. Releasing use, looking away, leaving range, or changing modes cancels an unfinished collapse. Rift mode never activates travel.

Saved Rift Locks
Locks, their order, and the convergence center survive logout and reload. Mode changes preserve the cycle. Capture, collapse, or successful travel clears the completed cycle; use /rt reset to abandon it deliberately.

Travel Mode
Activates an existing stabilized blue Convergence Rift. Aim at the blue portal from within ten blocks and hold Right mouse to synchronize. Travel mode cannot scan or harvest rifts, preventing accidental teleportation during collection.

Residue Extraction Mode
Recovers stored Temporal Residue.

Anchor Mode
Controls travel to the player's charged Travel Anchor.

Cargo Mode
Tracks Cargo Anchors, binds Cargo Transmitters, and controls shipments.

See Temporal Triangulation and Rift Travel for complete operating instructions, or Convergence Gates for constructed portal operation.
